title: Learning reveals invisible structure in low-rank RNNs
abstract: arXiv:2605.04115v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Learning in neural systems arises from synaptic changes that reshape the representations underlying behavior. While low-rank recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have emerged as a powerful framework for linking connectivity to function, a theoretical understanding of their learning process remains elusive. Here, we extend the low-rank framework from activity to learning by deriving gradient-descent dynamics directly in a reduced overlap space. We formulate a closed-form, low-dimensional system of ODEs that governs learning in this space, exact for linear RNNs and asymptotically exact for nonlinear RNNs in the large-$N$ Gaussian limit. Central to our analysis is a distinction between two classes of overlaps: loss-visible overlaps, which fully determine network activity, output, and loss, and loss-invisible overlaps, which do not affect function but are required to describe learning. translated_title: 学习揭示了低秩RNN中的不可见结构
translated_abstract: 神经系统中的学习源于突触的改变，这些改变重塑了行为背后的表征。虽然低秩循环神经网络（RNN）已成为连接网络结构与功能的强大框架，但对其学习过程的理论理解仍然难以捉摸。在此，我们将低秩框架从神经活动扩展到学习过程，通过在简化的重叠空间中直接推导梯度下降动力学。我们构建了一个封闭形式的低维常微分方程（ODE）系统来支配该空间中的学习，该系统对于线性RNN是精确的，对于大-$N$高斯极限下的非线性RNN是渐近精确的。我们分析的核心在于对两类重叠的区分：损失可见重叠（loss-visible overlaps），它们完全决定网络的活动、输出和损失；以及损失不可见重叠（loss-invisible overlaps），它们不影响网络功能，但却是描述学习过程所必需的。我们阐明了这种分解所带来的后果。
tldr: 本文推导出低维常微分方程系统来精确描述低秩RNN的学习动力学，并发现学习过程可分为决定网络功能的“损失可见重叠”和不影响功能但描述学习所必需的“损失不可见重叠”。
en_tdlr: This paper derives a closed-form low-dimensional ODE system governing gradient-descent learning dynamics in low-rank RNNs, revealing a decomposition into loss-visible overlaps that fully determine network function and loss-invisible overlaps that do not affect function but are required to describe learning.
